result.question: Why does the king think Arameans left?

readings.answer: Because they know we are starving.
readings.support: They know we are starving, so they have left the camp
they have left the camp to hide in the field

readings.answer: To take them alive and enter the city.
readings.support: When they come out of the city, we will take them alive and enter the city

assessments.reason: The text explicitly says, “They know we are starving, so they have left the camp,” giving the Arameans’ knowledge of Israel’s famine as a causal reason for leaving, though it does not state the ambush/conquest purpose emphasized in the key.

“They have left the camp to hide in the field” is a stated purpose for leaving and aligns with setting an ambush, though it does not explicitly include the further goal of entering/conquering the city.
“When they come out… we will take them alive and enter the city” matches the key’s idea of ambushing the Israelites and conquering the city.

result.reason: The verse gives both a causal reason (“they know we are starving”) and a tactical purpose (“to hide, capture them alive, and enter the city”), so materially different answers fit the question’s “why.”
